intent.instructions: You are choosing for a rolling scrap mech in a roguelite stage. The rules: the player damages an enemy only by landing on it from above, or by ramming it while above the fast speed tier. A difficulty tier rises every 45 seconds of stage time and raises enemy health, spawn rate and cache prices. Opening a cache spends the scrap its option states and grants one random buff that stacks and lasts the rest of the run. Scrap is spent only on caches. Health regenerates starting 5 seconds after the last hit, and the run ends at 0 health. The stage is cleared by holding a 60 second exit charge at the exit. Each option is an action available right now, with what it involves. Choose the single intent to hold for the next second or two.

danger.instructions: How close is the player to being hit, given current health and the listed threats?
criteria: Clear: no listed threat can reach the player in the next few seconds
Contested: a listed threat can reach the player in the next few seconds
Critical: a hit that a listed threat can land in the next few seconds would bring health to 0

greedy.instructions: If the player spent the next second or two taking reachable loot or a cache, would a listed threat or hazard reach the player during that time?

rationale.intent: Mechanics only: what each action does, what it costs and which clocks run. q1's intent carried two conclusions, "speed is what makes combat possible" and "scrap still held at the end of the run bought nothing" (audit A1). q2 keeps the rules those sentences rested on (damage only from above or from a fast ram; scrap is spent only on caches) and drops the conclusions. It asks for "the single intent", not the best one: the options state their costs and the choice is Jev's.
rationale.danger: Kept because buildQuestions sends it and decide.mjs reads its answer, so dropping it needs a harness change outside JL-18. q1's criteria said what to optimise ("free to optimise purely for speed and loot") and when a hit "matters"; q2's criteria describe reach and remaining health only. Recorded for analysis; no decision reads it (audit A18).
rationale.greedy: Kept for the same reason. q1 asked whether loot would "cost more, in rising difficulty and risk, than the value it adds", which supplies the costs and asks only for their sign; its answer read above 0.5 on every case while caches were taken (audit A7, A18). q2 asks a state question with no valuation: whether a listed threat or hazard reaches the player in the time the loot takes. Recorded for analysis; no decision reads it.
